programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann's murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann's notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt: Children in Need
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain's biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2's OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network's Nikita Kanda and Radio 1's Maia Beth. Let's hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here. Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey – black-necked swans. Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace – a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves. As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable – they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before. As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres. Her bold breeding colours signal she is looking for a mate, but late to the party, she must fight for one in the most peculiar way – by engaging in mouth-to-mouth combat. When spring gives way to summer, temperatures at the coast can rise by 50C in a matter of weeks. Living for just one year, a female octopus oliveri must capitalise on the summer bounty of Japan's rock pools whilst surviving the intense heat. But other octopuses dominate the pools close to shore. In an incredible feat, she pulls herself out of the water and walks on land. But as the heat of the day intensifies, she finds herself far from the water she requires to breathe. Can she make it back before she suffocates? On the Mediterranean coast in summer, the number of people can double. But 50 metres deep in the waters off Corsica, another gathering occurs. Picarel fish create a ten-million-strong supercolony of fish nests across miles of seabed. Here, a father must defend his precious eggs from hermit crabs, sea cucumbers and even other male picarel fish. Against all odds, a few thousand eggs survive an onslaught of cannibals – a job well done by a tenacious dad. At the peak of summer, seagrass meadows can grow ten times thicker than in winter, creating a dense home and feeding ground for many marine creatures. In the lagoon system of the Ria Formosa in Portugal, a long-snouted seahorse tries to find love. But what was once a vast grassland is now an eerily barren world, having been decimated by anchors and fishing boats. The search for a mate seems hopeless, but a lifeline in the form of a "seahorse hotel" created by scientists provides him with a sanctuary and a chance to find a new mate. The oceans are being changed not just by the seasons but by us. Winter waves hit the coast of Chile, washing newborn pups from their colony. Unable to swim, they become stranded. What's more, extreme storms are now four times more common there. But there is hope – committed volunteers aid the return of these helpless pups to the colony to be reunited with their mum. It's autumn in New York City. Thanks to fishing quotas being set in 2013, billions of menhaden fish now swarm along America's busiest coastline, drawing in charismatic marine characters – bottlenose dolphins, sharks and even ocean giants. Once a rare sighting in the waters surrounding the Big Apple, now up to 150 humpback whales feast on the menhaden shoals throughout spring, summer and into autumn. It's a sign that the animals of the seasonal seas show remarkable adaptability and a ray of hope in a rapidly changing ocean. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: The Future of Deaf Education.
programme.desc: Marios Costi presents a programme exploring deaf education: where it began, how it has changed and what the future could hold for the next generation. Marios is joined by Martine Monksfield, teacher of the deaf, former president of Batod and long-standing campaigner for improvements in deaf education. Together, they discuss the changes taking place across education, the importance of language and communication, and the need to protect the rights of deaf children, including those with additional needs. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four friends – in this episode, Jacqui, Nigel, Phil and Jane – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Edith Bowman go in search of tips and treats at the York Food Festival, including homemade hummus and the many surprising varieties of the English apple. Father of toddler triplets Onkar Singh Purewal is on the hunt for healthy food the whole family will eat. Ryan Hand gets to grips with Japanese cuisine, and chef Julie Lin reveals some affordable seafood. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo crosses the Culloden Viaduct aboard the Caledonian Sleeper to arrive bright and early in the coastal city of Inverness, from where he heads north on a magnificent scenic adventure to the Orkney archipelago. On boggy moorland overlooking the Moray Firth near Inverness, Michael explores the battlefield at Culloden, where Bonnie Prince Charlie's Jacobite army fought British government troops in 1746. Today, ponies and cattle help to preserve the character of the landscape as it was 275 years ago. Michael learns to execute the infamous Highland Charge and discovers how the Jacobites' catastrophic defeat devastated the Highlands for years to come. Excellent sea and rail links and swathes of lush pine forest in this coastal region have given rise to a strong timber industry. Michael investigates the production of oriented strand board for the construction industry at an Inverness mill, which manufactures 16 million boards annually. The Highland mainline climbs the Slochd summit to deliver Michael to the village of Carrbridge, home of the World Porridge Making Championships. At stake is a golden spurtle – does Michael's whisky-flavoured mushroom porridge risotto stand a chance? At Broomhill, Michael's dreams come true when he is invited to join the crew of the Strathspey Steam Railway on the footplate of their wonderful locomotive as they puff and pant their way past the River Spey and the Cairngorm mountains along the original main line from Inverness to Perth. At Aviemore, Michael heads into Cairngorms National Park to admire its epic scenery. On the banks of Loch Morlich, he learns about writer, poet and naturalist Nan Shepherd, who captured the essence of the Cairngorms in her prose. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: This series charts the contrasting fortunes of British fishing boats over the course of one brutal week. Each skipper must hunt the catch 24/7 if they are to earn a wage for themselves and their crew. It's the most dangerous job in Britain, and failure means risking your life for no reward. In this episode, it's the last trip before Christmas and, with demand surging, fish prices are rising. Off the south coast of Cornwall, Ocean Pride is heading out in pursuit of pollock among the old sunken shipwrecks of the English Channel. 380 miles away on the Yorkshire coast, crabber Tydus is preparing to head out with hopes of a big pay day. The aim is to put six tons in the tank, a catch that this week could fetch well over £30,000. Off the south coast of Devon, Margaret of Ladram, one of Brixham's most successful beam trawlers, is on the hunt for one of the most lucrative species in British waters, Dover sole. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the ancestral home of the Spencer family, Althorp in Northamptonshire. Nineteen generations have lived here, employing local people to work at the house and vast estate. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Christina is drawn to a 1950s toy pedal car, and Will finds a Mouseman tray. Paul Martin discovers how the Grand Union Canal was the waterway equivalent of the M1 as he takes to the water on a narrow boat and discovers what life was like for the boat people who ferried cargo from A to B. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Tim Whewell reports from eastern Libya, where a vast reconstruction programme led by the Haftar family is transforming cities and reshaping the country's political future. As new roads, housing projects and landmarks emerge, we examine whether stability and development are outweighing concerns about accountability and democratic change. Plus: we follow Zaher, a young Sudanese boy whose life was changed by war when a drone strike left him severely injured. A year on, we meet him in Cairo as he learns to walk with prosthetic limbs and begins rebuilding a childhood interrupted by conflict. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: The Peelers are back. While patrolling Belfast city centre, Dave and Owen stop a suspected drug dealer. They find a wad of cash and cocaine. The man claims he is a drug user struggling with addiction and, from the back of a cell, tells Stephen about his life. But when speaking to the custody sergeant, he lets slip a crucial detail that confirms Dave's suspicions. Next, reports come in of two men fighting on the street – each claiming to be the victim. After speaking to eyewitnesses and CCTV operators, Anna brings both into custody. On the way, one of the men launches a torrent of abuse at the Peelers. In west Belfast, the vehicle crime team – Dennis and Chris – are on shift and notice a car being driven erratically round a bend. When stopped, the driver, who is known to the team, tries to charm his way out of trouble. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: Harriet
programme.desc: Sie ist eine unerschrockene Frau: „Ich würde auch den letzten Tropfen meines Blutes geben, bis dieses Monster Sklaverei tot ist“, sagt Harriet. Maryland, 1849: „Minty“ Ross und ihre Familie sind als Sklaven an die Besitzer einer Plantage gebunden. Als sie verkauft werden soll, wagt sie die Flucht nach Pennsylvania, wo die Sklaverei für unrechtmäßig erklärt wurde. Dort nimmt sie den Namen Harriet Tubman an, kehrt nach einem Jahr in Sicherheit zurück, um auch ihrer Familie zur Freiheit zu verhelfen. Als Mitglied der Underground Railroad, einem aus Sklavereigegnern bestehenden Netzwerk — führt sie unter dem Codenamen Moses über 70 Menschen in die Freiheit. \n\nUS-Regisseurin Kasi Lemmons („Talk to Me“) erzählt die außergewöhnliche Lebensgeschichte als spannendes Abenteuerdrama, das von einer umwerfenden, 2020 für den Oscar nominierten Cynthia Erivo („Bad Times at the El Royale“) getragen wird. Vor allem Harriets persönliche Reise in der ersten Hälfte sorgt für ganz große Emotionen.

programme.title: See Hear: The Future of Deaf Education.
programme.desc: Marios Costi presents a programme exploring deaf education: where it began, how it has changed and what the future could hold for the next generation. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. But fluctuating prices, rising costs and the ever-present threat of disease have left many dairy businesses under financial pressure. Alongside local farmer Emily McGowan, Charlotte Smith and Adam Henson explore how dairy farmers across County Antrim, one of Northern Ireland's most productive dairy regions, are turning to tech and innovative business models to build a more resilient future. Adam also introduces this year's BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Every chef dreams of a Michelin star. Episode two of Rise of the Rockstar Chef follows the hunt for that recognition, and for the leap that separates the great from the legendary. Moving from one star to two is hard, but the hardest jump of all is from two to three. Marco Pierre White made that leap, becoming the first British chef to win three Michelin stars, and the youngest ever to do so. The episode explores what the pursuit demanded and what it cost. Marco reflects on the price of perfection. and how success also brings a rupture. Gordon Ramsay, who learned his craft under Marco, leaves to build his own name, and both men look back on the emotion of that parting. When menus from Aubergine begin appearing on Marco's desk, the friendship is over. Gordon recounts the story of the stealing of the restaurant's reservation book, the crown jewels of any restaurant, revealing just how bitter the split became. Marcus Wareing, Gordon's first employee, recalls the early days of Gordon's kitchen and the fierce ambition driving it. As the 90s unfold, Heston Blumenthal's drive, creativity and uncompromising pursuit of excellence transforms modern British cuisine. Heston cooks in a completely different way, and his food blows minds. It is pure theatre, with equipment unlike anything seen in a normal kitchen. Dishes such as the triple-cooked chip, taking two years to perfect, went on to change not just food but kitchens in restaurants and at home. With the opening of The Fat Duck, his home is on the line, and the need for success is huge. Meanwhile, the empires expand. Marco and Gordon take over the kitchens of some of London's top hotels, and their restaurants become the places to be. Marco's restaurant Titanic draws the Spice Girls, Oasis, footballers and the tabloids, with as many as 4,000 guests passing through in a single night – a 90s Studio 54. Contributors describe the energy of those years, and the revolutionary push for creativity in ways never seen before. When Heston is crowned the number one chef in the world, he voices the immensity of the pressure, his inferiority complex and the highs and lows of extreme success. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there's no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it's married couple Wendy and Phil, who don't plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it's friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there's no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn't pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Clive Myrie's Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: In Cuba's capital, Clive realises his boyhood dream of taking on a potential Olympic champion at one of Havana's legendary boxing gyms. He visits a car mechanic to get under the hood of a classic Chevy and finds out why most cars in Cuba are pre-1959 models. He also follows in the footsteps of the Buena Vista Social Club to discover how Cuban rhythms conquered the world. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. The microbiologists are back, this time facing a returning family of stargazers. The series has reached the knockout stage: one team will go home, but not before they've pondered the link between such clues as fore, dog, anti and woebe. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: Deaf Parenting
programme.desc: Tammy Broskom presents a programme exploring parenting: the challenges, joys and unexpected experiences of raising children. Families come in all shapes and sizes, and throughout the programme, parents share their stories as well as the advice and the lessons they have learned along the way. Tammy is joined by Michelle Goodwin, a deaf mum, teacher and advocate for deaf families. Michelle and her wife are raising two daughters, one hearing and one deaf. They discuss their journey to parenthood, their experiences of family life and the importance of communication, making sure both children feel included and connected. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's four members of the same family, Suraj, Nisha, Tina and Rob. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Edith Bowman visit the National Ploughing Championships in Derbyshire on a food adventure, where they discover the story behind the Bakewell tart and are let loose on tractors. Farmer Meinir Howells reveals the secrets of one of the UK's oldest ice cream parlours, Ryan Hand finds out the superpowers of seeds, and farmer Jim Smith learns the art of pickling. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning today on the Moray Firth, Michael admires the impressive Cullen viaduct before enjoying a bowl of Cullen skink at a family-run fishmonger of 150 years' standing. In the factory smokery, he learns from the owner how the famous soup acquires its distinctive taste. Heading west along the firth, Michael reaches Forres Station and the seaside village of Findhorn, where he meets members of an eco-community founded in the 1960s. At the Findhorn Foundation, Michael discovers spiritual energy, sacred dancing and a history of very large vegetables. Michael's next destination is Ardersier and the mighty Fort George, which sits on an isolated spit of land jutting west into the firth. Its huge boundary walls and heavy guns at every approach are an awe-inspiring sight. Michael hears why it was built on this coast in the mid-18th century and the role it has played in Britain's strategic defence, which continues to the present. He meets members of the Black Watch, part of the Royal Regiment of Scotland, who are based at the fort today. He also listens to a pipe and drum rehearsal and is permitted by Scotty the tailor to try on the regimental sergeant major's jacket. Nestled in woods next to the River Nairn, Michael discovers a romantic Scottish tower house, Cawdor Castle. Guided by Lady Cawdor, Michael discovers the castle's literary connections to a tragic Scottish hero. On the castle lawn, around the cauldron, Michael joins the witches to hail Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Off the coast of Yorkshire, Siwrengale is heading out for the beginning of the North Sea whelk season. Skipper Darren Warters is on the hunt with sons Regan and Lewis. Asian demand has created a lucrative fishery in this small patch of the North Sea, but winter storms have badly damaged their pots. Miles of rope must be untangled before they can begin fishing in earnest. South east of Shetland is "Long Hole" – the deepest waters in the North Sea. Reliance III is the only boat for miles around. In this secret spot, skipper John Clarke is hunting for whiting. But the whiting trade is one of the most volatile in fishing. When his grounds are discovered by rival boats, John is forced to move on. Endeavour 5 is far off in the North Atlantic, hunting for squid along the continental shelf. The brand new £8m boat was part-financed by a huge bank loan and built to withstand the toughest conditions off Scotland's west coast. When the squid prove elusive, the pressure starts to mount. But could the arrival of a winter storm see Endeavour's rivals forced back to harbour, giving it a monopoly over the squid grounds? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: At the historic Blackpool Tower Circus, Paul Martin is joined by experts James Lewis and David Fletcher. Between them, the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectibles to be sold at auction. James discovers a collection of watches that have been in the back of a wardrobe for years and David finds a pistol dating back to the Battle of Waterloo. But will a collection of military medals outdo them both? Paul also takes a look around Lancashire's oldest family home and its collection of antiques, amassed by 14 generations of the same family. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Strictly It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor dishes up some more unmissable backstage action from the world of Strictly. Some of the couples drop by for a chat about their next performance as they prepare to battle it out in the infamous Tower Ballroom. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Our Lives: Workhorse
programme.desc: This short documentary follows Kate Mobbs-Morgan and her trusty team of working horses. For centuries, horses formed an integral part of our working landscape. Kate is passionate about working horses and believes they still have a key role to play in today's environment. Kate trained in horticulture and always loved working with animals. In her late thirties, she was diagnosed with a rare cancer and had to undergo radical surgery. This prompted Kate to pursue a new career, combining her passion for working outdoors with her interest in working horses. Almost two decades later, she has built her own working-horses business, specialising in forestry work and land management. She and her horses are brought in to work on sites where large machines cannot gain access or are not wanted, such as locations that are environmentally sensitive, steep terrain and wet ground. Her horse-logging team is made up of: Kipp, the herd leader whom Kate has known since the day he was born but is now approaching retirement; Quinlan, who is powerful but suffers with anxiety; and Garth, a relatively new member of the team who has yet to start working full-time. There was a fourth member of the team, Sol, who passed away suddenly last year, leaving Kate heartbroken and the herd out of balance. To restore the herd to full strength, Kate has just brought in a young mare named Brigid, but she is quite feisty, and it will take several years of patient training before she is ready to join the other working horses. Kate knows that if there is to be a future for working horses, there needs to be people with the knowledge and skills to do the job. Alongside other professional horse loggers, Kate has started training new entrants into the industry. The working-horse community is relatively small and is spread out across the country. Once a year, though, horse loggers come together to compete. In 2026, the competition is being held in Yorkshire. An obstacle course will test both horse and handler, with contests for single horses and pairs. Kate takes her trusty steed Kipp and his anxious but sturdy companion Quinlan along to compete, but can she keep her own anxiety in check? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Match of the Day Wales: Wales v Portugal.
Rise of the Rockstar Chef

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As Bill's 75th birthday approaches, brother Joel joins the adventure, bringing some Murray family rivalry to the golf course. Comedian Joanne McNally attempts her first ever round, while a bouncing boat trip to the Cliffs of Moher brings further unexpected encounters. Then friends and familiar faces gather to celebrate a milestone birthday – and a reflective Bill looks ahead to what might come next. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: Deaf Parenting
programme.desc: Tammy Broskom presents a programme exploring parenting: the challenges, joys and unexpected experiences of raising children. Families come in all shapes and sizes, and throughout the programme, parents share their stories as well as the advice and the lessons they have learned along the way. Tammy is joined by Michelle Goodwin, a deaf mum, teacher and advocate for deaf families. Michelle and her wife are raising two daughters, one hearing and one deaf. They discuss their journey to parenthood, their experiences of family life and the importance of communication, making sure both children feel included and connected. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: In the second week of the heats, a fresh group of professional chefs wait in the wings of the kitchen ready to demonstrate their exceptional talent. All six are committed to their goal of securing a place in the quarter-final, but two huge challenges stand in their way. The competition gets underway with the skills test, but this time the chefs must cook side by side. Monica challenges them to create a technically demanding artichoke tarte tatin, testing their precision, timing and ability to keep cool under pressure. For some, its unfamiliar territory, and they'll need to think on their feet to avoid coming unstuck. Others draw on experience to rise to the challenge, but who will turn out a dish worthy of the pass? Next up, the signature dish round, where the six contestants must showcase their individual culinary identity, combining exceptional flavour with the technical mastery and finesse expected of a professional chef. They may have honed their dishes in the familiarity of their own kitchens, but delivering them to the highest standard under the intense pressure of the MasterChef kitchen is an altogether different challenge. Marcus and Monica face the difficult task of deciding who has done enough to progress, and for one chef ambition threatens to overwhelm their dish. The judges are looking for refinement as much as flair, but sometimes less really is more. Only those who can marry ambition with precision will secure their place in the competition. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher's house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks! (Senderinfo).

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: Marcus and Monica are joined by special guest Alex Claridge, the chef behind The Wilderness in Birmingham, whose eclectic, unconventional style combines bold flavours, unexpected ingredients and inventive techniques. Now, he's setting the chefs the challenge of recreating a dish that demands extraordinary precision: a sashimi of Cornish gurnard, lightly cured and accompanied by delicate pear, finished with a tare, smoked sesame emulsion and a jelly veil of oxtail consomme. This is a dish where subtlety is everything. For some of the chefs, the ingredients and techniques are entirely unfamiliar, and with no recipe to follow, they'll need to draw on their experience, trust their seasoned palates and remain composed under pressure. With a place in the quarter-final at stake, can they rise to Alex's exacting challenge, or will this intricate test prove a step too far? The final test is a sweet one, and the chefs must turn their attention to dessert, where precision and timing are crucial, and there is little room for error. Marcus and Monica are looking for more than perfectly executed patisserie. They want to see flair, imagination and a clear sense of each chef's style, all brought together in a dessert worthy of the MasterChef kitchen. It's a chance to finish on a high, but one mistake could undo all their hard work. As the final plates reach the pass, who will wow the judges, and whose MasterChef journey will end here? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: Finding Wellness
programme.desc: See Hear explores wellbeing and what it means to live a healthy, balanced life. Presenter Marios Costi shares practical advice on reducing stress, finding calm and making positive changes while meeting inspiring deaf people who are breaking down barriers, building confidence and pursuing their dreams. Marios talks with Avril Langard-Tang, a senior lecturer at the University of Wolverhampton and the first deaf woman to walk solo from John O'Groats to Land's End. She reflects on her extraordinary 980-mile journey, the physical and emotional challenges she faced and the support she received from the deaf community along the way. (Senderinfo).

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. This time, it's four members of the same family, Kathryn, Rab, Francis and Jan. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Edith Bowman introduces Colin Murray to her home town of Anstruther in Fife on a food adventure. As well as its famous fish and chips, they discover how artisan bread is being made for the community. Briony May Williams bags bargains hunting for yellow stickers in the supermarket, and chef Suzie Lee reveals how Greek-style yoghurt is made in County Down. Onkar Singh Purewal discovers Swansea's community garden produce. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's Scottish coastal railway journey reaches Invergordon on the Cromarty Firth, the third great inlet on the northeast coast of the Highlands. He arrives on Britain's northernmost railway, the Far North Line, and heads straight onto the water to explore a former oil drilling rig now moored in the firth. It's easier said than done; Michael is hoisted into the air by crane as he clings to a 'personnel basket'. The decline of the oil industry since its peak in the 1990s means that rather than drilling wells, this rig now caps old ones, securing them with cement. Michael helps to assemble a pipe that could stretch up to two miles long. Michael's next stop is Fearn, from which he heads to the mudflats and saltmarsh of Nigg Bay and its Global Energy Park. Michael hears how both the area and personnel have moved away from oil and gas to renewables and marvels at the colossal scale of the wind turbines he sees being readied for transport offshore. He discovers the blades for one tower are longer than a standard football pitch! On the shore of the Dornoch Firth, Michael helps to reintroduce his favourite delicacy to the firth's shallow waters. Oysters were plentiful in this region for thousands of years, but their great popularity during the 19th century led to a catastrophic decline. Now oysters are beginning to flourish again, and Michael joins Herriot Watt University's team effort to establish 200,000 oysters at Dornoch within the next three years. Michael's next stop is the Glenmorangie Whisky Distillery, also located on the banks of the Dornoch Firth. The science and art of whisky production are revealed to Michael as he tours the distillery. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Scalloper Golden Promise is pushing force-6 winds to get to newly opening scallops beds ahead of his rivals. With the boat first to the grounds, they are in for a big pay day – but only once they cover the £8,000 fuel expenses to get here. Family-owned trawler Adenia leaves Lerwick aiming to land 1,000 tonnes of mackerel in Norway in just three days' time. Shetland skipper George Anderson has 11 crew, eight of whom are family, and he is hoping the fish will meet the grade to sell into the lucrative Asian sushi market. If it does, George and the crew could be in for a million-pound pay day. Skipper Ivan Toms and 25-year-old son Rhys fish Maxine's Pride, one of the smallest and oldest trawlers in the UK fleet. In recent years, fishing has been a struggle, with little money to reinvest in the 35-year-old boat. Fishing Cornwall's inshore waters – reserved for smaller fishing boats – can they catch enough to give themselves a wage and put money aside for repairs? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are in Leicester where the 100-year-old De Montfort Hall plays host to their valuation day. Antiques experts Catherine Southon and Claire Rawle are hunting through the crowds for the finest antiques and collectables to take to auction. There are some real gems to see as they go under the hammer. Plus Paul Martin discovers that local radio was born right here in Leicester. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mortimer and Whitehouse: Gone Fishing.
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. They navigate the area through the lens of a six-year-old Bob as he takes Paul on a trip along the landscapes of his youth. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear to him are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner, who has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Pain is a fact of life. For many, it is excruciating and inescapable, a truly disruptive force. But amid the continuing fallout of the global opioid crisis, new technologies are being developed every day to limit and potentially even eliminate pain. Professor Hannah Fry learns about the future of pain management and how revolutionary technologies are being developed to directly control pain signals. She talks to the scientists behind these technologies about how this unprecedented breakthrough works, as well as meeting pain research participants themselves in order to understand the life-changing implications of such research. Along the way, she considers how society views pain and what a pain-free future would truly mean for humanity. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life: The Best Bits.
programme.desc: The rollercoaster has been sending our hearts racing and stomachs dropping for over a century, and today, millions of us get our kicks on these topsy-turvy, daredevil joyriders. Hannah gets the inside story on the UK's newest, tallest and fastest rollercoaster – Thorpe Park's Hyperia. She uncovers the wild origins of the modern-day coaster and finds out how some dodgy French physics in the 19th century, Nasa rocket scientists and an ambitious cartoonist called Walt delivered the ultimate thrill machine. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: First into the barn is Gary from Hastings, bringing his father Jimmy's old butcher's bike. Built for heavy loads, it was used to carry boxes of meat through Hastings in the 1950s before becoming part of Jimmy's wider life on the seafront, where he worked as a fisherman and later as a 'boy ashore', helping boats land their catch. Tragedy struck in the infamous storm of 1987, when Jimmy perished while trying to save fishing boats from the violent seas. Soon after, his friends created the Crown Lane bike race in his honour, with Jimmy's old delivery bike at the centre of the event. For nearly four decades, thousands of competitors have pedalled the heavy machine uphill for charity, but years of wear have left it unsafe to ride. Bike restorer Tim Gunn sets about strengthening its frame, fixing brakes and cranks, and ensuring it is safe for the future, while Dom Chinea adds a new hand-painted advertising board to honour Jimmy's memory. Next, father and son Paddy and Gary travel from Belfast with a prized pair of motorcycle racing goggles belonging to Paddy's father, George Brockerton. George was an extraordinary competitor who began his motorbike journey as a teenage dispatch rider in the First World War before becoming a celebrated racer. He competed in the Ulster Grand Prix, the Isle of Man TT, and in 1935 became the only known Irishman to win a coveted Brooklands Gold Star after breaking the 100mph barrier – a feat almost unheard of at the time. His goggles, once a symbol of daring speed and personal pride, have deteriorated, their brittle latex eyepieces crumbling with age. Shoemaker Dean Westmoreland and plastics expert Charlotte Abbott join forces to carefully recreate the missing parts, preserving the distinctive shape and colour so that Paddy and Gary can once again celebrate George's achievements. From Mid Wales, Amanda arrives with a mysterious painting known as The Last Gathering, found in the attic of her family's farmhouse near Mynydd Epynt. The artwork captures a rural ritual, where farmers would bring livestock down from the mountains for shearing and selling – a practice that ended abruptly when the community was evicted during the Second World War to make way for a Ministry of Defence training ground. For Amanda, whose family has farmed in the area for generations, the painting represents not just history but a lost way of life. Paintings conservator Lucia Scalisi begins by surface-cleaning but soon discovers areas of overpainting that conceal hidden details, including a key element obscured for decades. Through careful restoration, she uncovers the lost figure and revives the painting's original balance, reconnecting Amanda and her sons to a story their community still treasures. Finally, sisters Lyndsay and Karen bring in a very personal piece of childhood history – Puffin, a miniature toy boat built for them in the early 1980s by their late father. Crafted during his lunch breaks at the bus repair works using scrap materials from buses and workshops, the boat was the centre of the sisters' childhood play. Decades later, it became a source of joy for their own children, but years of play and weather have left it broken and unsafe. Woodworker Will takes on the task of rebuilding the rotten bow, dashboard and seating, while upholsterer Sonnaz contributes a playful finishing touch. Together, they ensure Puffin can be cherished not only as a family keepsake but as a tangible link between grandchildren and the grandfather they never met. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Murder Case: Fire in the Suburbs
programme.desc: On New Year's Eve in 2016, 23-year-old university student Cameron Logan and his girlfriend, 24-year-old journalist Bex Williams, are celebrating the new year. After partying into the small hours at a friend's house, they walk home together to Cameron's family home in an affluent suburb of Glasgow, where they were staying overnight. In the early morning of 1 January, Bex and Cameron wake in terror with their bed on fire, and, within seconds, flames have engulfed the entire room. Telling her story fully for the first time, Bex Williams recalls the horror of those initial moments. Crawling through the smoke and flames in search of a way out, she tries to escape through the kitchen but discovers the back door is locked. In a remarkable act of ingenuity, she opens the freezer and puts her head in, just before losing consciousness. Cameron's parents are woken by the chaos and manage to escape with minor injuries, and Bex is pulled to safety and rushed to hospital. Cameron's older brother Blair returns home to find his family home overcome by fire, with firefighters and police already at the scene. This is just the beginning of the horror story for Bex and the Logan family, as Cameron has not made it out alive. Once the fire is brought under control, detectives and forensic experts begin to examine the scene. What initially appears to be a devastating house fire soon takes a sinister turn. Inside the property, investigators discover the unmistakable smell of petrol, and Cameron's mother says she saw a masked figure throw something into the living room where Cameron and Bex were sleeping, before fleeing the property. Police Scotland's Major Investigation Team is now faced with a murder case and a baffling question: why would anyone target this family? With the clock ticking, the team begin to meticulously piece together the evidence from the scene and build a picture of the events of that night. With no obvious motive to investigate, detectives must follow every lead as they try to understand what really happened inside this family home. Meanwhile, Bex is in intensive care fighting for her life and is put in a medically induced coma. As soon as she wakes, detectives are keen to speak to her. Did she witness what happened, or know who the masked figure was? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories – reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: New York New York
programme.desc: Auf einer rauschenden Siegesfeier zum Kriegsende 1945 verliebt sich der Tenorsaxofonist Jimmy (Robert De Niro) in die kecke Francine (Liza Minnelli). Er überredet sie, in seiner Band zu singen und seine Frau zu werden. Als Francine ein Kind erwartet, kommt es zum Streit um die künstlerische Aufrichtigkeit: Der introvertierte Jimmy spielt in Nachtclubs den schrägen Bebop, Francine zieht eingängigen Swing vor. Sie trennen sich, und Francine macht Karriere… \n\nScorsese erzählt die Liebesgeschichte eines Musikerpaares, das die Zerreißprobe zwischen Kunst und Käuflichkeit nicht besteht. Die Hommage an die Swing-Ära ist zugleich eine Parodie auf die MGM-Musicals. Der Soundtrack stammt von John Kander und Fred Ebb (beide komponierten für „Cabaret“), De Niros Sax-Double ist Georgie Auld.

programme.title: VIP Trip – Prominente auf Reisen 6
programme.desc:
Die Halbinsel Istrien und die dalmatinische Küste – Kroatien ist stets eine Reise wert. Umso mehr, wenn Sie mit einem Wohnmobil unterwegs sind. Schauspieler und Synchronsprecher Oliver Hörner hat für Sie einige der schönsten Campingplätze des Landes angesteuert: direkt am Meer, mit schattigen Stellplätzen und einem üppigen Freizeitangebot.

Begleiten Sie uns auf die exklusive Insel Brijuni und das facettenreiche Eiland Pag mit seinen berühmten Pager Spitzen, dem würzigen Schafskäse und natürlich: seinem Salz.

Doch Kroatien hat noch mehr zu bieten: ausgedehnte und unberührte Waldlandschaften. Streifen Sie mit uns durch den Nationalpark Risnjak in Gorski kotar mit seinen glasklaren, türkis-schimmernden Bächen. Kommen Sie mit auf unserer Fahrt im Wohnmobil durch Kroatien – der Natur ganz nah. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Faszination Elbrus – der Ritt zum Gipfel
programme.desc:
Planet Weltweit:

Über Jahrhunderte wurden die robusten Karachai-Pferde im Kaukasus gezüchtet, doch vor rund 50 Jahren galten sie als fast ausgestorben. Lokalen Züchtern ist inzwischen gelungen, den Fortbestand dieser Tiere zu sichern. Der Pferdezüchter Hasan Salpagarov will nun den Elbrus, den höchsten Gipfel auf über 5600 Metern, per Pferd besteigen.

Die saftigen Hochweiden im Nordkaukasus bieten den riesigen Herden der Karachai-Pferde genug Nahrung. Die Pferderasse gehört schon seit jeher zu dieser Region. Doch Stalins Säuberungspolitik der 1930er-Jahre brachte Zehntausenden Menschen Tod und Vertreibung. Viele Nordkaukasier kehrten nie aus Stalins Gulags zurück. Um die Karachai-Pferde kümmerte sich kaum noch jemand, ihr Bestand nahm immer weiter ab, das Aussterben schien nur noch eine Frage der Zeit zu sein.

Doch die Rückbesinnung auf die kaukasische Identität und die Liebe zur Heimat sorgten für ein Comeback der Karachai-Pferde, hier am Fuße des Elbrus. Bereits 1999 erreichte eine Gruppe Wagemutiger mitsamt Pferd den Gipfel. Diesen spektakulären Aufstieg will Pferdezüchter Hasan zusammen mit seinen beiden Brüdern jetzt wiederholen, als Symbol für das Wiedererstarken seiner besonders robusten Pferde.

Trotz seiner atemberaubenden Schönheit bleibt der Kaukasus ein mächtiges, Respekt einflößendes Gebirge. Der höchste Berg, der Elbrus, ragt über 5600 Meter in die Höhe. In der Stadt Ust-Dscheguta soll die Expedition starten, über Zwischenstationen und Basislager im Laufe mehrerer Tage bis ganz nach oben.

Aber bevor es losgehen kann, brauchen die beiden Expeditions-Pferde noch spezielle Hufeisen. Schmied Wassili weiß genau, worauf es im Hochgebirge ankommt. Am Elbrus herrschen extreme Bedingungen. Die Tiere müssen auf Schnee- und Eisflächen unbedingt sicheren Tritt fassen können. Wird der Gipfel tatsächlich noch einmal mit Pferden zu bezwingen sein? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Wanderlust!
programme.desc:
Ein Geheimtipp in der Wanderszene ist der E4 auf Kreta. Der Fernwanderweg quert die größte Insel Griechenlands von West nach Ost. Am schönsten ist es im Südwesten, wo das Bergmassiv der „Levka Ori“ 2.500 Meter hoch aufragt und steil ins Meer stürzt.

Bradley Mayhew ist mit der kretischen Wanderführerin Penelope unterwegs. Denn der „Europäische Fernwanderweg Nr. 4“ ist auf Kreta nicht überall gut markiert. Bradley hat sich 230 Kilometer vorgenommen.

Der Pfad beginnt auf den Höhen der Westküste. Weit reicht der Blick aufs tiefblaue Meer, bevor Bradley und Penelope absteigen und im Kloster Chrissoskalitissa vorbeischauen. Zwei Stunden später sieht es aus wie in der Karibik: Türkis leuchtet das Meer in der Lagune Elafonissi. Die beiden hängen die Bergschuhe über den Rucksack und wandern knietief durchs Wasser.

Dann ist die Südküste erreicht. So steil fallen die Bergflanken ins Meer, dass für Straßen kein Platz ist. Nur per Schiff oder wandernd kommt man voran. Charakteristisch für Kreta sind die tief eingeschnittenen Schluchten, die Berge und Küste verbinden.

Penelope führt Bradley die Samaria-Schlucht hinauf: 1.200 Meter Anstieg auf 18 Kilometer Länge. Abends in den Bergen werden die Wanderer zu Lamm und Rotwein eingeladen und lauschen den Rizitika-Gesängen der Männer.

Bradley muss alleine weiter. Er steigt auf zur Berghütte Kallergie und quert in zwei Tagen die Levka Ori, die Weißen Berge. Beim Dorf Aradena trifft er Marianna, die ihn durch den Canyon von Aradena begleitet. Die Schlucht wurde von Rebellen als Versteck genutzt.

Sfakia heißt die Region. Die vielen Eroberer Kretas – Byzantiner, Sarazenen, Osmanen – haben sie nie völlig kontrolliert. Das Schöne an Kretas Schluchten: Sie führen direkt zum Meer.

So endet der Tag für Bradley an der klitzekleinen Marmara-Bucht, mit bestem Essen und einem Sprung ins Meer. Genusswandern! In Bradleys Hitliste der schönsten Wanderwege Europas steht Kreta ganz weit oben. (Senderinfo).

programme.desc: Die Großfragant ist ein sehr beliebtes Wander- und Skitouren-Hochtal in den Hohen Tauern, welches für Touristen nach wie vor eher einen Geheimtip darstellt, da es prinzipiell nur zu Fuß erreichbar ist, und auch etwaiges Gepäck für eine Übernachtung nur durch eine schon recht in die Jahre gekommene Seilbahn nach oben transportiert werden kann. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Heimatleuchten

(Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Das Red Bull Erzbergrodeo bringt die Fahrer:innen an ihre Grenzen. Der Vorjahressieger Manuel Lettenbichler trifft 2024 auf den aufstrebenden Newcomer Mitch Brightmore. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Entstehung der Alpen
programme.desc: Entstehung der Alpen – Schatzkammer Alpen: Unsere Alpen sind eine wahre Schatzkammer, sogar im allerengsten Sinn des Wortes. Denn unter den Wurzeln der Berge schlummern wertvolle Ressourcen. Der österreichische Wissenschafter Prof. Rudi Simek ist dafür durchs Land unterwegs auf der Suche nach diesen Schätzen. Stets mit einem Augenzwinkern, ob in den Mythen nicht doch ein Kern Wahrheit steckt. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Faszination Elbrus – der Ritt zum Gipfel
programme.desc:
**Planet Weltweit:**

Über Jahrhunderte wurden die robusten Karachai-Pferde im Kaukasus gezüchtet, doch vor rund 50 Jahren galten sie als fast ausgestorben. Lokalen Züchtern ist inzwischen gelungen, den Fortbestand dieser Tiere zu sichern.

Der Pferdezüchter Hasan Salpagarov will nun den Elbrus, den höchsten Gipfel auf über 5600 Metern, per Pferd besteigen. Die saftigen Hochweiden im Nordkaukasus bieten den riesigen Herden der Karachai-Pferde genug Nahrung. Die Pferderasse gehört schon seit jeher zu dieser Region.

Doch Stalins Säuberungspolitik der 1930er-Jahre brachte Zehntausenden Menschen Tod und Vertreibung. Viele Nordkaukasier kehrten nie aus Stalins Gulags zurück. Um die Karachai-Pferde kümmerte sich kaum noch jemand, ihr Bestand nahm immer weiter ab, das Aussterben schien nur noch eine Frage der Zeit zu sein.

Doch die Rückbesinnung auf die kaukasische Identität und die Liebe zur Heimat sorgten für ein Comeback der Karachai-Pferde, hier am Fuße des Elbrus. Bereits 1999 erreichte eine Gruppe Wagemutiger mitsamt Pferd den Gipfel. Diesen spektakulären Aufstieg will Pferdezüchter Hasan zusammen mit seinen beiden Brüdern jetzt wiederholen, als Symbol für das Wiedererstarken seiner besonders robusten Pferde.

Trotz seiner atemberaubenden Schönheit bleibt der Kaukasus ein mächtiges, Respekt einflößendes Gebirge. Der höchste Berg, der Elbrus, ragt über 5600 Meter in die Höhe. In der Stadt Ust-Dscheguta soll die Expedition starten, über Zwischenstationen und Basislager im Laufe mehrerer Tage bis ganz nach oben.

Aber bevor es losgehen kann, brauchen die beiden Expeditions-Pferde noch spezielle Hufeisen. Schmied Wassili weiß genau, worauf es im Hochgebirge ankommt. Am Elbrus herrschen extreme Bedingungen. Die Tiere müssen auf Schnee- und Eisflächen unbedingt sicheren Tritt fassen können. Wird der Gipfel tatsächlich noch einmal mit Pferden zu bezwingen sein? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bergwelten
programme.desc:
Wie wird man mit der Leidenschaft Klettern alt und glücklich?

Die Antwort kennt niemand besser als der Vorarlberger Beat Kammerlander: indem man sich verändert und immer wieder neu (er)findet.

Zu seinem 65. Geburtstag lässt dieses außergewöhnliche Porträt nicht nur seine großen Leistungen in den steilsten Wänden Revue passieren. Es kommt Beat Kammerlander ganz nah, um die Kletterikone auch als Menschen greifbar zu machen.

Als einen, der zeit seines Lebens im extremsten Gelände unterwegs war und weder Tod noch Teufel fürchtete. Aber auch als jemanden, für den Harmonie und menschliche Beziehungen über allem stehen, der spät, mit 55 Jahren, zum ersten Mal Vater wurde und gezeigt hat, dass man seiner Leidenschaft auch nach einer solchen Metamorphose noch treu sein kann. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bergwelten
programme.desc:
Der Hohe Göll liegt zwischen Watzmann und Königssee im Westen und dem Salzachtal mit Salzburg im Osten. Quer über den 2.522 Meter hohen Gebirgsstock verläuft die Grenze zwischen Bayern und Österreich bzw. dem Salzburger Land.

In dieser Bergwelten-Folge erkunden wir den Hohen Göll im Winter. Kalendarisch beginnt er am 21.12. mit der feierlichen Wintersonnenwende. Dann folgen wir einem Berufsjäger in seinem Revier im Göll-Massiv. Gerade im Winter ist die Hege und Pflege des Wildes überlebenswichtig.

Der Hohe Göll ist auch ein grandioses Revier für Bergsportler: Wir erleben ein eisiges Canyoning-Abenteuer im Bluntautal, eine Überschreitung des ganzen Göll-Massivs auf Ski und eine extreme Ski-Abfahrt in der steilen Ostwand.

Wir besuchen das Salzbergwerk in Bad Dürrnberg und erfahren mehr über die Sage vom bösen Göll-Weib und dem Wetterbock. Denn der Hohe Göll ist ein Berg mit vielen Geschichten und eine ganze, spannende Bergwelt. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Über alle Berge – Mit Lamas über die Alpen
programme.desc:
Die Alpen – trotz ihrer Größe und Erhabenheit versuchen die Menschen es immer wieder, sie mit eigener Kraft zu bezwingen.

Zwei Männer aus Tirol machen sich auf den Weg, den schon der große karthagische Feldherr Hannibal vor mehr als 2000 Jahren gewagt hat: den Traumpfad. Über die Alpen von München bis nach Venedig.

Ein einzigartiges Abenteuer über 550 km Wegstrecke und über 20.000 Höhenmeter.

Ihre Weggefährten sind jedoch keine Elefanten – es sind zwei Lamas. Für Mensch und Tier eine unglaubliche Anstrengung. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: In the Face of Manaslu
programme.desc:
Im September 2012 machten sich fünf Männer auf den Weg in den Himalaja, um am Manaslu (8.163 m) einen Geschwindigkeitsrekord aufzustellen und als Erste vom Gipfel abzufahren.

Als eine Lawine das Hochlager trifft und elf Bergsteiger tötet, gehören die fünf Protagonisten zu den Ersten vor Ort und retten einige der verschütteten Überlebenden.

Doch kann man im Angesicht des Todes an seinen Plänen festhalten?

Zwei Mitglieder geben auf, drei steigen weiter in Richtung Gipfel. Nur einem gelingt schließlich die Abfahrt. Ein neuer Weltrekord wird aufgestellt – aber zu welchem Preis?

Im Angesicht des Manaslu entsteht ein Jahr nach der Tragödie eine eindringliche Standortbestimmung. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: In the Face of Manaslu
programme.desc:
Im September 2012 machten sich fünf Männer auf den Weg zu einem Geschwindigkeitsrekord im Himalaja, um den Manaslu (8.163 m) zu besteigen und als Erste abzufahren.

Als eine Lawine das Hochlager trifft und elf Bergsteiger tötet, sind die fünf Protagonisten die Ersten, die einige der verschütteten Überlebenden retten. Kannst du nun im Angesicht des Todes mit deinen Plänen weitermachen? Zwei Mitglieder geben auf, drei steigen zum Gipfel auf, nur einem gelingt die Abfahrt. Ein neuer Weltrekord wird aufgestellt – aber zu welchem Preis? Im Angesicht des Manaslu ist eine Definition des Standpunkts ein Jahr nach der Tragödie.

Im September 2012 machten sich fünf Kameraden auf, um bei einer Speedbegehung des Manaslu (8.163 m) in Nepal einen neuen Weltrekord aufzustellen.

Als das „High Camp“ einer Expedition von einer Lawine verschüttet wird und elf Bergsteiger in den Tod reißt, sind die fünf Kameraden als Erste an Ort und Stelle, um den Verschütteten zu helfen. Die Frage ist nun: Kann man nach solch einem Ereignis seine Pläne, den Manaslu zu besteigen, fortsetzen? Nur drei der fünf Männer machen sich auf Richtung Gipfel und stellen einen neuen Weltrekord auf. Doch zu welchem Preis wurde dieser Weltrekord aufgestellt? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bodensee – Wildnis am großen Wasser
programme.desc: Jeden Sommer zieht es Kulturinteressierte aus ganz Europa an den Bodensee. Kultur, Wasser und Natur – diese drei Elemente versprechen Festspiele der besonderen Art. Doch auch abseits der großen Bühne versammeln sich jedes Jahr unzählige Besucher. Auch sie kommen meist von weit her. Wie ein Magnet zieht der Bodensee Hunderttausende Zugvögel an. Ihre Routen ziehen sich quer durch Europa. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Life of Tao
programme.desc: "Life of Tao" ist eine packende Doku-Serie über den österreichischen Freeride-Profi Tao Kreibich, der in den Alpen zu Hause ist, aber seine Spuren in der ganzen Welt zieht. Die Serie verbindet Big-Mountain-Skiing mit authentischem Storytelling, Freundschaft und dem Abenteuer, immer neue Orte zu entdecken. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Planet Weltweit
programme.desc:
Noch vor wenigen Jahren waren Esel in Montenegro akut vom Aussterben bedroht. Dass es die einst auf dem Balkan zahlreichen, treuen Helfer noch immer gibt, ist vor allem Darko Saveljić zu verdanken.

2015 rettete der Biologe die erste Eselstute; die Besitzer hielten sie in elenden Verhältnissen. Kurze Zeit später nahm er zwei andere Esel zu sich, die als Futter für Jagdhunde geschlachtet werden sollten. Inzwischen sind es 59 Stuten und ein Hengst, die auf Darkos Eselfarm ein Zuhause haben – hoch in den Bergen, 17 km von Montenegros Hauptstadt Podgorica entfernt.

Mandarina ist mit 40 Jahren die älteste Stute auf der Farm. Bevor Darko Saveljić sie zu sich nahm, hatten ihre Besitzer sie als Arbeitstier ausgebeutet und dabei jahrelang nicht einmal bemerkt, dass sie blind ist.

Drina hingegen war das erste Fohlen auf der Farm, geliebt und verhätschelt von der ganzen Familie. Als ein Wolf ihre Mutter tötete, hielten die Saveljićs die Eselwaise umso mehr wie eines ihrer Haustiere. Doch als immer mehr Esel auf die Farm kamen, baute die Familie für die neuen Bewohner einen Stall und ein Auslaufgehege. Inmitten der Herde steht nun auch Drina – die nun jedoch umso eifersüchtiger darüber wacht, dass sie die meiste Zuwendung genießt.

Was als Rettungsaktion für die oft misshandelten und ausgesetzten Esel begann, ist zu einer überaus populären, amüsanten und zu Herzen gehenden Umweltschutzaktion des kleinen Balkanlandes geworden.

Noch vor 30 Jahren sicherten Esel den Bauern Montenegros das Überleben. Sie ackerten, bis Landflucht und Maschinen sie in den Augen ihrer Besitzer überflüssig und wertlos machten. Und obwohl der Esel zum kulturellen Erbe auf dem Balkan gehört, zählt er in Montenegro plötzlich zu den vom Aussterben bedrohten Tierarten.

Die letzten Esel davor zu bewahren und ihnen ein artgerechtes Leben zu ermöglichen sowie sein Modell von Tierschutz in die Öffentlichkeit zu tragen, dafür kämpft Darko Saveljic. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Wanderlust!
programme.desc: (D/F 2015). „Das Gehen in der Landschaft“ galt lange als langweilig, ist jetzt aber wieder voll angesagt. Reiseführerautor Bradley Mayhew stellt reizvolle Fernwanderwege in Europa vor, die auch Normalsportliche bewältigen können. Er startet an Italiens dramatischer Amalfiküste.

programme.title: Heimat Österreich
programme.desc: Spätestens ab 1. Mai steht in fast jeder Gemeinde Österreichs ein bis zu 30 Meter hoher geschmückter Baum, in manchen Orten sogar vor jedem Gasthaus. Dieser Film besucht die Steiermark und Oberösterreich und versucht zu erkunden, wie viel von dem alten Brauchtum noch lebendig ist. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Heimatleuchten
programme.desc: Heimatleuchten: Dachmarke von ServusTV, das das Heimatgefühl Österreichs transportieren soll. In verschiedenen Dokumentationen wird die österreichische Vielfalt präsentiert: die unterschiedlichsten Traditionen, prägende Landschaften, jahrzehntealte Bräuche, die Kulinarik und ungewöhnliche Geschichten über die Bewohner des Landes. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: Die Saison neigt sich dem Ende zu und Babsi Zangerl und Jacopo Larcher müssen bei eisigen Temperaturen unzählige schwierige Seillängen bezwingen, um zu beenden, was sie begonnen haben. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: Seb Bouins DNA (9c) besteht aus umgedrehten Fußdynos, kaum vorhandenen Griffen und endlosen Bewegungen in einer riesigen Höhle in Frankreich. Hier beweist Seb, dass er an der Spitze der menschlichen Leistung im Klettersport steht. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Wade Young will sich als unabhängiger Fahrer bei der Xross Hard Enduro Rallye 2024 und bei den Red Bull Romaniacs beweisen, nachdem er von seinem alten Team mit Teodor Kabakchiev ersetzt wurde. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Entstehung der Alpen
programme.desc:
Entstehung der Alpen – Erlebniswelt Alpen:

Unsere Alpen – seit jeher ein geschichtsträchtiger Ort im Herzen Europas und Mittelpunkt historischer Entwicklungen und bahnbrechender Erkenntnisse.

Beeindruckende Berge, wilde Flüsse und einzigartige Landschaften haben die Menschen seit Jahrhunderten bewegt und in die Alpen gelockt.

Prof. Rudolf Simek macht sich auf die Spuren des Tourismus. Warum kamen die ersten Reisenden in die Alpen, und wie entwickelte es sich zum Massentourismus? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Love of the Wild
programme.desc: In der abgelegenen Arktis Finnlands führen Aki und sein treuer Hund Äijä Angeltouren durch unberührte Gewässer. Aki und seine Partnerin Emilia haben das geschäftige Stadtleben gegen die wilde Schönheit jenseits des Polarkreises eingetauscht. Durch endlose Sommertage und lange, dunkle Winter passen sie sich den Extremen der Arktis an und meistern Herausforderungen von Polarnächten bis hin zum von Polarlichtern erleuchteten Himmel. Diese Folge beleuchtet Akis tiefe Verbundenheit mit dem Land und seine Mission, Finnlands traditionelle Fischereipraktiken zu bewahren. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bergwelten
programme.desc: Die Charakteristik der Julischen Alpen, dem österreichischen Grenzgebirge mit Meerblick zum Golf von Triest, ist geprägt von einem schroffen und steilen Gebirge, das besonders im Winter einen hohen Reiz für Alpinisten, Paragleiter, Freerider und alpine Skibergsteiger bietet. Alpine Abenteuer in den Julischen Alpen lassen sich am besten so beschreiben: Groß. Beeindruckend. Ernst. Einsam. Und mit viel italienischem und slowenischem Charme. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mit Mut und Motorsäge – Baumkletterer im Extrem-Einsatz
programme.desc: Tagtäglich trotzen österreichische Forstarbeiter voller Leidenschaft den Naturgewalten, um unter schwersten Bedingungen unsere Wälder zu pflegen. Der Wald ist ihr Zuhause, ihr Leben, ihr Schicksal. Tagtäglich trotzen österreichische Forstarbeiter voller Leidenschaft den Naturgewalten, um unter schwersten Bedingungen unsere Wälder zu pflegen. Der Wald ist ihr Zuhause, ihr Leben, ihr Schicksal. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Sagenhafte Extremkletterer
programme.desc: Der Film zeigt authentische, sensationelle Tieraufnahmen des Murauer Naturfilmers Klaus Illitsch und des Bad Gasteiner Försters und Jägers Thomas Tscherne. Mit der Kamera geht das WILDE LAND für Sie auf eine filmische "Pirsch". In Folge 3 sind wir sagenhaften Extremkletterern auf der Spur: den Gämsen. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Unrideables – Alaska Range
programme.desc: Speedriding ist eine rasante Bergsportart mit hohem Risiko, die Elemente des Skifahrens und des Gleitschirmfliegens miteinander verbindet. Dieser hybride Ansatz in der alpinen Umgebung ermöglicht es wagemutigen Sportlern, in ansonsten unzugängliches Gelände vorzudringen. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Wade Young will sich als unabhängiger Fahrer bei der Xross Hard Enduro Rallye 2024 und bei den Red Bull Romaniacs beweisen, nachdem er von seinem alten Team mit Teodor Kabakchiev ersetzt wurde. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Piemont – Mit Mulis über Stock und Stein
programme.desc: Es gibt ihn noch, den Beruf des Säumers – Menschen, die Lasten auf dem Rücken von Saumtieren durchs Gebirge transportieren. Jahrhundertelang beförderten sie Waren über schwer zugängliche Alpenpässe. In den Seealpen, im italienischen Piemont, liegt auf 2.300 Metern die Schutzhütte Morelli Buzzi. Drei Monate im Jahr muss der Betreiber der Hütte Wanderern Kost und Logis anbieten. Doch Wege und Straßen hier hoch gibt es keine, und den Helikopter kann sich der Hüttenwirt nur einmal in der Saison leisten. Da kommen Luciano Ellena und seine Mulis ins Spiel. Er ist der letzte Säumer im Piemont und versorgt die Hütte in den kommenden drei Monaten mit Lebensmitteln. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Wanderlust!
programme.desc: Bradley Mayhew empfiehlt nur, was er ausprobiert hat. Der britische Reiseführerautor marschiert durch Andalusien, von Tarifa nach Ronda. – Klasse Bilder, dazu Abstecher in Geschichte und Lebensart.

programme.title: Heimat Österreich
programme.desc: Die Sonnwende wird in der westlichen Welt vielerorts mit einem Feuerritual begrüßt, dessen Wurzeln bis tief in die Keltenzeit zurückreichen. Ein besonderes Erlebnis sind die Feierlichkeiten im Niederösterreichischen Nibelungengau zwischen Persenbeug und Melk. Hell beleuchtete Schiffe gleiten donauabwärts und passieren dabei einen Feuerzauber der auf den Hügeln abgebrannt wird. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Heimatleuchten
programme.desc: Heimatleuchten: Dachmarke von ServusTV, das das Heimatgefühl Österreichs transportieren soll. In verschiedenen Dokumentationen wird die österreichische Vielfalt präsentiert: die unterschiedlichsten Traditionen, prägende Landschaften, jahrzehntealte Bräuche, die Kulinarik und ungewöhnliche Geschichten über die Bewohner des Landes. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: Der Weltklasse-Kletterer Leo Houlding, die Kletterin Anna Taylor aus Cumbria und der Dschungel-Experte Waldo Etherington unternehmen eine Big-Wall-Expedition, um eine neue Route am überhängenden Bug des Mount Roraima zu finden. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: Nachdem die ersten drei Seillängen geschafft sind, muss die "Geheimwaffe" des Teams, Anna Taylor, die bisher schwierigste Seillänge bezwingen, um den Traum von der freien Begehung am Leben zu erhalten. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Beim 24MX Hixpania Hard Enduro – dem Saisonfinale 2024 – kommt es zu einem großen Showdown. Kann Manuel Lettenbichler erneut die Weltmeisterschaft gewinnen oder wird ein anderer den Titel holen? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Entstehung der Alpen
programme.desc: Entstehung der Alpen – Mythos Alpen: Unsere Alpen. Eine beeindruckende und vielfältige Landschaft, die über Jahrmillionen entstanden ist. Prägende Epochen und historische Ereignisse spielten sich ab, umgeben von imposanten Berggipfeln der Alpen. Aber woher stammen die vielfältigen Namen unserer Berge und Gebirge? Und welche Geschichten führten zu ihrer Benennung? Wenn die Berge unserer Alpen selbst sprechen und erzählen könnten, würde es lange dauern bis sie etwas über uns zu berichten hätten. Denn als der Mensch hier irgendwann einmal hier auftauchte, standen die Gebirge selbst schon Millionen von Jahren (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Piemont – Mit Mulis über Stock und Stein
